definition: A model trained to predict how much a human would prefer one output over another, used to provide a training signal for reinforcement learning from human feedback.
details: Reward models are typically trained on datasets of human comparisons between pairs of model outputs, and then used to score new outputs during the RL fine-tuning phase of alignment.
story: Picture a gambler who slowly learns which slot machines pay out, not by reading a manual but by pulling the lever. In plain words: A model trained to predict how much a human would prefer one output over another, used to provide a training signal for reinforcement learning from human feedback. Here is how it actually plays out: Reward models are typically trained on datasets of human comparisons between pairs of model outputs, and then used to score new outputs during the RL fine-tuning phase of alignment. The learner writes its own textbook from consequences. That learn-by-reward loop is Reward Model.
